flashcard_questions.q: A medical condition where a person has a BMI of 30 or above, caused by consuming more energy than the body uses over a sustained period.
Body Mass Index — a measure calculated by dividing a person’s weight in kilograms by the square of their height in metres. A BMI of 30 or above is classified as obese.
A state where the energy consumed from food and drink exceeds the energy the body uses through BMR and physical activity, leading to weight gain over time.

flashcard_questions.a: A condition where the coronary arteries that supply blood to the heart become narrowed or blocked by a build-up of fatty deposits (atheroma), reducing blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart muscle.
flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by 'coronary heart disease'?

flashcard_questions.a: A type of fat found mainly in animal products and some processed foods. Eating too much raises blood cholesterol and increases the risk of heart disease.
